section.title: Introduction
section.para: RelationAnnotator reads the token, entity, and dependency layers and writes RelationAnnotator.RELATIONS. Each RelationPattern names a relation type, a dependency path between subject and object entities, and an optional trigger word on the path. Extracted mentions carry subject and object entity indexes and a span covering the arguments in original text coordinates.

section.title: Pattern syntax
section.para: A path is a whitespace-separated sequence of steps. A step <label walks up from the subject entity's head token over an arc carrying that dependency relation, a step >label walks down toward the object entity's head token, and every up step must come before the first down step. A path therefore always runs from the subject up to a single pivot token, the lowest common ancestor of the two entity heads, and down to the object. The head of a multi-token entity is the first token overlapping the entity span whose own dependency head lies outside the entity.

The trigger is optional and constrains the pivot token: the pattern matches only when the pivot's lowercased form equals it. A null trigger accepts any pivot. A trigger is never rewritten, so it must already be lowercase and must not contain whitespace; anything else is rejected when the pattern is constructed.
